payload.purpose_context: Attendees of the upcoming Spec Kitty training need a short self-paced prep before the session: the basic vocabulary (agent, skill, doctrine, chatbot vs agentic) and a working setup of Git, Python 3.11+ and an AI coding agent, tailored by a short intake to their OS, hardware and tool. It is a standalone static site hosted on the trainer's GitHub Pages, so the live session can spend its time on spec-driven building instead of installs.
payload.purpose_tldr: A light, standalone pre-session e-learning so Spec Kitty class attendees arrive knowing the key terms and with Git, Python and an AI coding agent installed.

payload.question: Is the 4-module outline (Words you'll hear, Vibe coding vs spec-driven, Get set up, Ready check; ~30 min) the scope?
What language should the content be in?
Which platforms, hardware and AI coding tools must the setup guidance cover?

payload.final_answer: All operating systems, all hardware, all AI coding tools: generalized and tool-neutral

payload.question: Should the track start with a short intake questionnaire that tailors the content?

payload.final_answer: Yes, short intake that filters content; hosted on the trainer's GitHub Pages; every attendee gets an individual experience with no mixing between users

payload.question: Is this built inside the existing onboarding lab or as its own app?

payload.final_answer: A full new standalone repo and app; the onboarding lab was only context

payload.question: Which tech stack: vanilla HTML/CSS/JS static site with no build step (like the trainer's other apps), or a framework?
Should the course be open to anyone with the link, or behind a simple shared passphrase?

payload.final_answer: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, native ES modules, no build step, offline-capable; same as the trainer's other apps
Open to anyone with the link; no passphrase
